similar_scenes.name: Post-punk dub (On-U Sound)
similar_scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
similar_scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
similar_scenes.desc: El punk, el funk y el dub se entretejen: el estudio como instrumento. The Slits con Dennis Bovell, The Pop Group en Bristol y, sobre todo, Adrian Sherwood y su sello On-U Sound: New Age Steppers, African Head Charge (precursor del techno-dub) y Tackhead, banda de estudio que endureció el sonido hacia el funk industrial y politizado.

similar_scenes.name: Post-punk / art-punk
similar_scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
similar_scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
similar_scenes.desc: Tras el viaje de John Lydon a Jamaica nace el post-punk: PiL infecta de dub sus diatribas. El punk blanco se cruza con la música negra (A Certain Ratio, ESG, Liquid Liquid, Gang of Four, Shriekback, 23 Skidoo), Wire construye nuevos lenguajes, y Joy Division renace tras la muerte de Ian Curtis como New Order, que hermana post-punk y disco americana y prepara al Reino Unido para el house. Factory tuvo su propio club: The Haçienda.

podcast.title: Emergence in 1977
podcast.body: The year 1977 is considered the beginning of post-punk, alongside punk rock and New Wave, marking a significant shift in music after the earlier prolific years of rock. "1977 punk, the beginning of New Wave, the era of post punk and all that came with it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Frenetic Birth and Diversification (1977-1981)
podcast.body: The period from 1977 to 1981 was exceptionally frenetic in music history, witnessing the birth and ramification of numerous genres. Within this rapid diversification, Post-Punk emerged, with Joy Division's first album, *Unknown Pleasures*, considered a potential culmination and significant origin point for the genre. "Dentro de todo ese cúmulo de ramificaciones nace la semi del POSPANG y posiblemente el gran germen del POSPANG, es el primer disco de J-Division."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Term Coined in 1977
podcast.body: The term "post punk" emerged around 1977, coinciding with the peak of punk, to describe the music that came after it. It served as an umbrella term for a new sound that rejected traditional rock and roll norms but maintained a connection to punk's expressive freedom. "Ergo, the name post punk, which was an umbrella term for this music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 5: New Wave

podcast.title: 1978-1982 Music Industry Revolution
podcast.body: Between 1978 and 1982, the music industry underwent a revolution, seeing the birth of post-punk. "nacían el post-punk"

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Michael Jackson hizo el disco más vendido de la historia

podcast.title: Early Terminology Attempts (1978-1979)
podcast.body: As the original punk rock scene declined, writers sought new ways to categorize the evolving music. John Savage proposed "new music" (with a K) in late 1978, while Simon Frith tried to popularize "after punk" (one word) in spring 1979, but neither term successfully captured public imagination. "As the original punk rock scene ran down a number of people offered up new words. There was new music spelled with a K on the end."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Emergence from Punk Burnout (Late 1978)
podcast.body: By late 1978, the initial punk rock scene and its distinct sound began to wane. A new wave of underground music emerged that, while recognizing punk's influence, deviated significantly in sound, arrangements, instrumentation, fashion, and politics from bands like The Ramones and Sex Pistols, necessitating new descriptive terminology. "But by late 1978 the original punk rock scene in sound was beginning to burn out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Era Definition (1978-mid 80s)
podcast.body: The post-punk era, roughly spanning from 1978 to the mid-1980s, is characterized by sounds and styles that, while not punk, could not have existed without punk's initial impact, forming the foundation for the alternative revolution of the 1990s. "We now call this the post punk era. And this period of time, roughly from 1978 through to the middle 80s, created the foundations for the alternative revolution in the 90s and beyond."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 1: New Wave

podcast.title: First Print Usage (February 1978)
podcast.body: The phrase "post punk" first appeared in print in an article in the UK's NME magazine in February 1978, authored by Charles Shaar Murray. Paul Morley later adopted the term, integrating it into his reviews starting in 1980, which contributed to its broader acceptance. "The first time anybody can remember the phrase post punk being used in print was an article in the UK's NME magazine written by Charles Schar Murray in February of 1978."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Emergence in Early 1979
podcast.body: By early 1979, the original punk rock scene had largely dissipated, giving way to the era of post-punk, a period characterized by a rapid succession of new sounds and attitudes that could only have evolved in the wake of punk's initial emergence. "By early 1979, the original punk rock scene had pretty much burned itself out. And we entered the era of post punk, a time when it seemed like a new sound attitude came out every day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's the Big Deal About Joy Division?

podcast.title: 1981 - An Incredible Year
podcast.body: The year 1981 is highlighted as "one of the most incredible years" for the Post-Punk genre, indicating a period of significant output and innovation. "1981 fue uno de los años más increíbles del Postpank."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: 2000s Revival
podcast.body: The 2000s saw a new revival of Post-Punk, with bands like Bloc Party, Editors, and other new generation bands emerging. "Luego en el 2000 tuvimos ese nuevo rival del Post Punk en el que salían, pues, blockparti en el que salían los editoros, en el que salían todas estas bandas de la nueva generación del rival del Post Punk."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Especial JOY DIVISION: 4. La banda tras el final

podcast.title: Avant-Garde and Broadened Sounds
podcast.body: This genre delved into "deeper waters" than punk, pushing beyond traditional rock norms with an avant-garde style. It incorporated synthesizers, world music, funk, jazz, and dance music, drawing ideas from non-musical arts like cinema, literature, politics, and fashion. "It fished in deeper waters than punk. It went outside the norms of traditional rock. It was more avant-garde in style and thinking."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bowie's Lodger Album and Post-Punk
podcast.body: David Bowie's "Lodger" album, described as artsy and experimental, encompassed what was about to happen with new wave and post-punk music, influencing future groups like Talking Heads. "And taking as a whole, it again encompasses what was about to happen with new wave and post-punk music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bowie's Low Album's Impact
podcast.body: David Bowie's "Low" album became profoundly important to a new generation of kids in the post-punk era who sought musical directions beyond traditional guitar-driven rock, directly influencing bands like Joy Division. "Low became very important to a new generation of kids in the post-punk era who wanted to do something different than just play guitars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: British Innovators
podcast.body: British post-punk bands like Japan were known for their interesting musical explorations, including a shift towards electronic sounds. "one of the more interesting British post-punk bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Catch-all Term
podcast.body: "Post punk" emerged as a catch-all phrase for music that originated from the punk scene but did not sound like traditional punk. "The first was post punk. It was a catch-all phrase for the music that came out of the original punk scene, but didn't sound like punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Characteristics Compared to Punk
podcast.body: Post-punk differed from punk in several key aspects: it was more introspective and focused on personal experiences and suffering, whereas punk was overtly aggressive and outwardly hateful. Post-punk drew heavily from literature for inspiration, with artists like Ian Curtis, Siouxsie, and The Cure being notable examples. It prioritized sound quality, refined recording techniques, and featured more technically proficient musicians. Its influences were more complex, including Krautrock, Can, Pink Floyd, and The Velvet Underground, making it more intricate than the raw and sometimes musically precarious punk. "el post-punk por otro lado era como otra vertiente muy distinta, no era tan odiada hacia el mundo era como mucho más introspectivo, hablaba mucho más de vivencias personales, ha dado mucho más de sufrimiento personal, tenía mucha influencia en la literatura"

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Especial JOY DIVISION: 1. Inicios en la escena post-punk

podcast.title: Closer as a Post-Punk Masterpiece
podcast.body: Joy Division's album *Closer* is regarded by many purists as the definitive masterpiece of the entire post-punk genre. "closer sí que es la verdadera obra cumple de todo el post-punk."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Especial JOY DIVISION: 3. Closer y la muerte de Ian Curtis

podcast.title: Complexity and Experimentation
podcast.body: This new music, unlike previous genres, was characterized by its complexity and experimental nature, unusual in its inspiration, tensions, construction, composition, and execution, moving beyond the simple two- or three-chord punk songs. "This new music was unlike anything that had come before it. It seemed more complex and experimental. Not necessarily complicated when it came to playing it, but certainly unusual in its inspiration, its tensions, its construction, its composition, and its execution."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: DIY Tenets
podcast.body: The central tenets of the "do it yourself" ethos from punk rock ingrained themselves into many other genres loosely grouped under the umbrella of post punk. While these sounds were not strictly punk, the influence of punk was clearly discernible. "And the central tenets of doing it yourself, engraved itself into many other genres loosely grouped under the umbrella of post punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Defined by What it is Not
podcast.body: Similar to other emerging genres, post punk is often most easily defined by what it is not: the "lugubrious, intricate, wady" sound that characterized progressive rock. "It's almost easier to define these categories by what they are not. Lugubrius, intricate, wady."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Defining Legacy
podcast.body: Post-punk left a lasting legacy that defined electronic music, alternative music, and independent music for the following three decades, effectively completing the revolution initiated by punk. "El Pospang dejó un legado que definió la música electrónica, la música alternativa y la música independiente que vendría en las tres siguientes décadas."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: La traición que salvó al punk. PiL

podcast.title: Defining Theme: "I'm F'd"
podcast.body: A succinct way some defined the core thematic difference of post-punk, in contrast to punk's confrontational "FU" stance, was "I'm F'd." This encapsulates the genre's often darker, more complex, and introspective exploration of existential angst. "Some people put it this way. If punk was all about FU, post punk's main theme was I'm F'd."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Definition
podcast.body: Post-punk describes all music that was encouraged by the punk explosion after roughly 1977 or 1978. "Post-punk is the most common term. That's easy to figure out. It's all the music that the punk explosion encouraged to happen after 1977 or 78 or so."

podcast.title: Definition and Origin
podcast.body: "Post-punk" describes a sound or band that isn't punk rock but could not have existed without punk coming first, indicating an evolved but similar DNA. It is the oldest of the "post-" prefixed terms. The first recorded use in print was in the British magazine Sounds in 1977, to describe Siouxsie and the Banshees. "In the case of post punk, for example, the term is used to describe a band or sound, which isn't punk rock, but listening to them, you could tell that punk had happened."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Definition and Origins
podcast.body: Post-punk emerged around the same time as punk (1977-1978), leading to questions about whether it is a genre that truly "comes after" punk or rather a distinct interpretation of punk's fundamental ideas. Joy Division, while not inventing post-punk, became its ultimate expression and a leading exponent. "posiblemente el post-punk no se algo que viene después del punk sino una interpretación distinta de las mismas bases que tenía el punk."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Definition by Simon Reynolds
podcast.body: Music writer Simon Reynolds defined post-punk as "music that wasn't punk, but you could tell by listening to it that punk had to have happened," signifying music that emerged in the wake of the original punk rock explosion. "The best definition of post-runk that I've ever read and I think this comes from music writer Simon Reynolds is music that wasn't punk, but you could tell by listening to it that punk had to have happened."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Doubts on Definition and Delimitation
podcast.body: There are still doubts about whether "Post-Punk" is the correct term and how to properly delimit it, as the bands within the genre were quite heterogeneous and diffuse. "Y aún tenemos dudas de que se acorre tu llamarlo Post Punk. O tenemos ciertas dudas de muy bien cómo delimitarlo, era bastante virogénio en las bandas, era como bastante difuso."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Duration of the Era
podcast.body: Post-punk was prevalent from approximately 1979 through the mid-1980s, before the music scene became too splintered to be encompassed by a single umbrella term. "Post Punk was a thing from about 1979 through to the mid 1980s, before things got splintered and segmented so much that we needed a whole bunch of new categories."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Eastern European Revival
podcast.body: The distinctive, dark, and danceable sound pioneered by bands like Kino, influenced by brutalist architecture and the coldness of Leningrad, has been rediscovered and embraced by the new wave of post-punk bands in Eastern Europe, such as Molchat Doma. "Una de N sonoro que ha recuperado la nueva ola del post-punk de Europa del Este. Bandas actuales como los vio los rusos Molchat Doma son herederos directos de esta atmósfera."

podcast.body: Post punk was one of the eclectic genres explored by The Police, the band that made Gordon Sumner (Sting) famous. "In the police, the eclectic post punk band that made him famous, Sting wrote all of the hits and tried his hand at punk, reggae, new wave, synth pop, and romantic balladry."

podcast.title: Effectiveness and Criticism of the Term
podcast.body: The term "post punk" proved effective for distinguishing groups like Joy Division and Gang of Four from conventional punk, particularly among UK bands. However, some found the term "a little too elitist or vague," prompting the search for alternative descriptors. "It worked quite well, especially with groups like Joy Division and Gang of Four and several others out of the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Emergence in Spain
podcast.body: Post-punk arrived in Spain as an evolution of punk, which, despite its initial impact, began to stagnate. It expanded punk's disruptive attitude with a more experimental approach, integrating influences like dub and electronics, exploring deeper themes. "El post-pank surgió en la terra como una evolución del punk cuando se vio que este último a pesar de su impacto inicial comenzaba a estancarse."

podcast.title: Emergence of Gentler Bands
podcast.body: As the 1970s transitioned into the 1980s, the post-punk era witnessed the emergence of a new wave of bands that consciously moved away from loud guitars and aggressive vocals. These groups presented a significant departure from the soft rock that had previously dominated mainstream charts, instead offering a cool, arty, and often melancholic romanticism. They frequently recorded introspective songs, sometimes in their own bedrooms, for independent labels, thereby laying crucial groundwork for the development of Tweetpop. "And as the 70s turned into the 80s, the post punk era, bands who didn't yell over loud guitars began showing up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evolution from After Punk
podcast.body: In the early 1980s, as alternative and underground movements sought specific names, the genre initially known as "After Punk" later adopted the name "Post Punk." This marked a diversification from the broader "New Wave" umbrella. "teníamos el After Punk que después se le llamaría Post Punk."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Evolution from Punk
podcast.body: Following the punk rock explosion of the mid-1970s, punk's angry guitars gave rise to a diverse range of post-punk sounds. This music, while distinct from punk, clearly showed its origins and influence. "The punk and its angry guitars begin a variety of post-punk sounds. This music wasn't punk, but you could tell by listening to it that something like punk must have happened."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evolutionary Link
podcast.body: The Post-punk sound of the early 1980s evolved through the mid-80s Shoegaze movement, which utilized heavy and distorted guitar work, eventually transforming into the modern indie music known today, including Grunge. "como ese sonido del post-pandelo de primeros de los 80 se convierte en la música indie moderna tal y como la conocemos."

podcast.title: Experimentation in the Early 1980s
podcast.body: Following the original punk rock era, the post-punk period was marked by extensive experimentation. This led to a diverse range of new sounds, often facilitated by advancements in electronic technology like more powerful synthesizers, drum machines, samplers, and sophisticated recording equipment.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Indie Generation Label
podcast.body: Post-punk is one of the names used to describe the first significant generation of indie music, which emerged between 1978 and 1982 and included bands like Joy Division, R.E.M., The Cure, and The Smiths. "mucha gente todavía no lo llama música indie sino que lo conocemos muchas veces como Postpank."

podcast.title: Forefathers of Alternative Rock
podcast.body: In the late 1980s and 1990s, the advent of alternative rock led to these "post punk forefathers" being regarded as seminal figures, akin to "Beatles forefathers." "the advent of alternative rock in the late 80s and 90s treated them like beatless forefathers."

podcast.title: Goth and Dark Stuff Movements (Early 1980s)
podcast.body: The early 1980s saw the rise of significant post-punk movements like Goth and Dark Stuff, which established a distinctive musical and fashion aesthetic. These scenes were characterized by dark moods and correspondingly black attire, with bands such as The Cure becoming internationally recognized for embodying this style and sound. "In the early 1980s, one of the great post-punk movements was known as Gough, Dark Stuff, and the fashion was as black as the mood of the music."

podcast.title: Gothrock Origin
podcast.body: Gothrock is identified as one of the longest surviving genres that emerged from post-punk. "Goth Rock may be one of the longest surviving of all the post punk genres."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Guitar Sound on Low
podcast.body: Post-punk guitars were a significant element on tracks like "Speed of Life" and "Be My Wife" from David Bowie's 1977 album 'Low'. This influence, combined with electronic music and Brian Eno's ambient sound, marked Bowie's departure from his earlier styles during his experimental "Berlin period." "It bore a heavy influence from electronic music and Brian Eno's ambient sound, as well as post-punk guitars on tracks like Speed of Life and Be My Wife."

podcast.title: Impact of Punk on Music
podcast.body: The post-punk era was a period where "older music had been shaken by punk so much that people were more willing than ever to find new paths." This indicates that punk rock fundamentally disrupted established musical norms, opening up new creative directions. "The older music had been shaken by punk so much that people were more willing than ever to find new paths."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Independent Label Dominance
podcast.body: During a significant period of Post-Punk, independent record labels were primarily responsible for the majority of new releases, indicating a time when major labels missed significant musical trends. "una parte importante del PostPunk, las discográficas independientes fueron casi las que coparon los lanzamientos de gran parte del PostPunk."

podcast.title: Influence from David Bowie
podcast.body: David Bowie's album "Low" became very important to a new generation of kids in the post-punk era who sought to move beyond guitar-centric punk styles. His experimental and synthesizer-driven music offered a different path, influencing bands like Joy Division. "Low became very important to a new generation of kids in the post punk era who wanted to do something different than just play guitars, punk style."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influences from Pre-Punk Avant-garde
podcast.body: Post-punk drew heavily from music that was previously disliked by the punk scene, including reggae, Krautrock, Tim Buckley ballads, and Captain Beefheart's experimentation. "Música codiaba la escena punk, pero que poco después, serían una gran referencia para el post-punk."

podcast.title: Introspective Message
podcast.body: In the late 1980s and early 1990s, Post-Punk was largely characterized by introspective messages that frequently conveyed personal feelings of sadness, misunderstanding, and frustration. This self-focused lyrical content stood in contrast to the outward-facing, combative messages brought forth by bands such as Rage Against the Machine. "Todo el mensaje del Grunge y de muchas bandas que teníamos de finadro de los 80 y primero de los 90 nos pesaba un poco con esos mensajes que teníamos el post-punk. Quenan todo yo, yo, yo, yo, yo, yo, yo, yo, yo estoy triste, yo no entiendo, yo estoy frustrado, yo tengo celos, yo estoy triste, yo estoy triste, yo estoy de premido."

podcast.title: Key Artists and Styles
podcast.body: Artists and styles considered post-punk include David Bowie's "Low" album, goth, dark wave, dream pop, jangly guitar bands like R.E.M., spiky groups like Wire, shoegaze, and Brian Eno's solo ambient experiments. "David Bowie's low album from 1977 ticked all those boxes. [...] Goth, dark wave, dream pop, the jangly guitars, bands like R.E.M., the spiky stuff of groups like Wire and Shoegay's were, and in some cases still are, artists in those buckets that we can consider to be post-punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Killing Joke's Apocalyptic Beliefs
podcast.body: The English post-punk band Killing Joke released their album "Revelations" in 1982, drawing inspiration from the biblical apocalypse. Following its release, singer Jaz Coleman became convinced that the world was about to end and, along with guitarist Geordie, relocated to Iceland to await the cataclysm. "Killing Joke was a very heavy post-punk band from England and in 1982 they released an album called Revelations and yes it was inspired by the apocalypse as described by St. John in the Bible."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Kraftwerk's Influence Questioned
podcast.body: The question is posed whether post-punk would be the same without Kraftwerk, indicating their significant influence on its development. "Serían lo mismo el rock-proredesivo, el post-punk, o incluso el hip hop?"

podcast.body: The Police's song "Message in a Bottle" from "Regatta de Blanc" was described as "Skah meets Post Punk," illustrating a blend of influences within their sound. "In the UK, the album's first two singles were both number 1 hits, the Dub Reggae style walking on the moon, and the Skah meets Post Punk message in a bottle, whose romantic lyric found Sting brooding about how loneliness was like being a star."

podcast.title: Mid-Decade Punk Revival Style
podcast.body: Post Punk was identified as a key style categorizing the mid-decade punk revival of the 2010s, alongside Garage Punk. This revival, possibly influenced by political events, represented a diverse range of approaches from bands like Against Me!, Sleater-Kinney, Japandroids, Fucked Up, Parquet Courts, Idles, and Sleaford Mods, building on previous punk eras. "If there's a way to categorize that mid-decade revival in Punk, it would perhaps be Garage Punk and Post Punk."

podcast.title: Mod Revival Adoption
podcast.body: During the mod revival of the 1970s, some post-punk bands embraced mod attitudes and aesthetics. The Jam, notably, was the biggest band to bridge these two styles. "Some post-punk bands adopted mod attitudes and aesthetics, and the biggest of them all was the jam."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: New Levels of Musicianship
podcast.body: Post-punk musicianship was elevated by bands like the Talking Heads, who, with the help of producers like Brian Eno, created slinky and funky grooves that showcased rhythmic complexity. "Thanks in part to producer Brian Eno, the group created some pretty slinky and funky grooves which took post-punk musicianship to new levels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Not Just Dark and Gothic
podcast.body: Post-punk is more than just a sound or a genre; it was not solely dark and gothic music, nor merely what followed punk. It represented "the greatest period of openness and creativity in music history." "Es por eso que el Pospang no es solo un sonido ni un genero, no fue solo música oscura y gotica... sino que supuso nada a la setra parte de mayor apertura y creatividad de la historia de la música."

podcast.title: Origin of Goth and Industrial
podcast.body: The post-punk era, beginning in the late 1970s, was a time when punk's influence encouraged diverse musical experimentation, leading to the emergence of both Goth and Industrial music with their distinct dark sounds and sensibilities. "We call this the post-punk era, and some of the very first bands from this era were into dark sounds and sensibilities."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Punk Sounds
podcast.body: Post-punk was a diverse era that spawned various styles, including Goth, Technopop, Industrial, and Modern Skah, all largely British inventions. These sounds emerged, spread, and often died quickly. "the birth of all the different styles that followed in the wake of punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Punk – Not a Genre but a Collection of Genres; Punk Had to Happen First
podcast.body: Post-punk is not itself a genre but describes a collection of genres that followed punk. These genres did not necessarily sound like punk, but something like punk had to have happened for them to emerge. The variety of music within the post-punk sphere was enormous. It was not blues-based like mainstream rock — it was punk-based. "Post-punk describes a collection of genres that followed punk. These genres didn't necessarily sound like punk, but something like punk had to have happened for these sounds to have emerged."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Recent Invention
podcast.body: The concept of Post-Punk itself is considered a relatively recent invention due to its late coinage and ongoing definitional ambiguities. "Entonces, el propio concepto de Post Punk es un inventor relativamente reciente."

podcast.body: Simon Frith's book, "Rip It Up and Start Again, Post Punk 1978 to 1984," is recommended for those wanting to explore the concept of New Wave and Post Punk in depth. "There's an excellent book on the whole concept of New Wave and Post Punk called Rip It Up and Start Again, Post Punk 1978 to 1984 by Simon Frith."

podcast.title: Recording in Old Church Halls
podcast.body: Post-punk bands, along with punk bands, frequently utilized Wessex Studios in North London, an old church hall that provided a "really live sound" for their recordings. "A lot of punk bands and post punk bands, like using the place, the clash and the damned and suzy and the banshees and the pretenders and the specials and generation X and the sex pistols."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Refinement of Ramones' Approach
podcast.body: Following the burnout of many early, angry punk bands, post-punk groups emerged. These bands refined the melodic and pop-oriented songwriting style that The Ramones had pioneered, evolving the sound in new directions. "There was a whole group of post-punk bands that took what the Ramones were doing and refined it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reinterpretation by Interpol
podcast.body: Interpol successfully reinterpreted post-punk, infusing it with their own personal vision. This approach allowed them to evolve while maintaining a unique identity, influencing other bands like the Arctic Monkeys who are now exploring similar retro influences. "Cuando los interpol reinterpretaron el post-punk le dieron su propia visión, una visión personal."

podcast.title: Rejection of Avant-garde Labels
podcast.body: While the music was avant-garde, terms like "avant-garde" or "postmodern" were deemed too pretentious to describe the burgeoning scene. "It was definitely avant-garde, but you couldn't call it that. That was way too pretentious. Postmodern? No, same thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Relatively Recent Term
podcast.body: The term "Post-Punk" is relatively recent, having started to be used extensively in the late 1980s and early 1990s, much later than the period it describes. "Incluso, el propio concepto de Post Punk es relativamente reciente. Lo hemos aguñado bastante más tarde de lo que pues posicionamos el Post Punk."

podcast.title: Shift to Synthpop
podcast.body: In 1982, the sound of new wave underwent a significant transformation from its earlier powerpop and post-punk origins to embrace synthpop. This evolution was heavily influenced by the emergence of slicker and more expensive music videos, signaling a "changing of the guard" in the musical landscape. "changing the very sound of new wave from Powerpop and Postpunk to Synthpop."

podcast.body: Post-punk had a strong historical presence in Bristol, contributing to the city's diverse musical tradition. "el gijob y el post-punk."

podcast.title: Survivors Scoring Pop Hits
podcast.body: By 1984 and 1985, many "post-punk survivors of the late 70s" were successfully scoring pop hits, largely due to the exposure and popularity generated by MTV and radio. This period marked a commercial resurgence for artists who had emerged from the post-punk era. "all of the post-punk survivors of the late 70s were scoring pop hits."

Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Technological Fragmentation
podcast.body: Beyond MTV's influence, new technologies for composing, performing, and recording music contributed significantly to the further growth and fragmentation of post-punk music, leading to new stylistic variations. "This contributed to the further growth and fragmentation of post-punk music."

podcast.title: Thematic Exploration
podcast.body: One particular current within post-punk delved into themes of alienation, nihilism, and the gothic, giving rise to bands like Joy Division, Siouxsie and the Banshees, The Cure, Bauhaus, and Killing Joke. This darker facet was central to the Spanish "onda siniestra." "Una de esas corrientes exploró la alineación el nihilismo y logótico. De esta vertiente más oscura surgieron bandas como J-Division, Suixi and the Abansis, The Queer, Bauhaus o Killing Joke."

srcs.episode: La España Siniestra ｜ La edad de oro del Postpunk y el Dark wave

podcast.title: Tony Wilson's "Postmodern" and its Link
podcast.body: Tony Wilson, founder of Factory Records, introduced the term "postmodern" to describe the new music his label championed, such as Joy Division, aiming to connect it with the aesthetic of actual postmodernism in art. Other writers, including Charles Shaar Murray and Paul Morley, interpreted "postmodern" as an abbreviation for "postmodern punk," which eventually shortened to simply "post punk." "This phrase was postmodern and he applied it to groups like Joy Division."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transformed by Krautrock
podcast.body: Krautrock's entry into the UK music scene, facilitated by British labels, had a significant impact, transforming the sound of post-punk music in the country. Its influences are clearly audible in bands like Joy Division and New Order. "This is how crop rock started to make serious inroads into the UK, inroads that changed post-punk music in the country."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transition to Manchester Sound
podcast.body: The Post-Punk era is characterized by a "sad and depressive history" with slow, sometimes dark rhythms. The Manchester movement marked a shift away from this, with bands making music that was more joyful, danceable, agile, and electronic, featuring happier lyrics and faster rhythms. "dejan un poco esa historia un poco triste y depresiva del post-punk y esos ritmos a veces un poco lentos y luego brez que tenían el post-punk para hacerlo como más alegre, más bailable, más agile, más movido, un pelín más electrónico, tenemos ahí esas letras más alegres y esos ritmos más rápidos"

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Umbrella Term for Late 1970s Rock
podcast.body: Post-punk served as an umbrella term for rock music of the late 1970s, characterizing a period where musicians, freed by punk's stripping down of rock, built things up again with new tools and attitudes. "Post-punk was an umbrella term for rock music of the late 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Undefined Nature
podcast.body: Post-punk is cited as an example of a musical movement that is difficult to define and delineate, similar to the challenges in distinguishing between shoegaze and dreampop, due to its heterogeneous elements. "también nos pasa con el post-punk yo he división a post-punk, de que el post-punk eran lo mismo, no, entonces es como que a veces nos pasa esos movimientos un tanto heterogenios que no son fáciles a cotar y definir."
